## Design

This experiment checks the sensitivity of the Tables 1–3 Ky–Fan permutation test to population means, using fixed $k=1,3$. It retains $(p,m)=(10,50),(10,150),(40,150)$, C1–C4, and all 15 N/T/E/G/L distribution pairs: 180 base scenarios.

Generate zero-mean samples $X_i^{(0)},Y_i^{(0)}$ with the original procedure, then set

$$X_i=X_i^{(0)}+\mu_X,\qquad Y_i=Y_i^{(0)}+\mu_Y.$$

Deterministic shifts preserve population covariance, so all cases satisfy $\Sigma_X=\Sigma_Y$. Let $e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top$ and $\mathbf1_p=(1,\ldots,1)^\top$.

| Case | $\mu_X$ | $\mu_Y$ | Purpose |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `baseline` | $0$ | $0$ | Zero-mean Tables 1–3 baseline |
| `common_shift` | $c\mathbf1_p$ | $c\mathbf1_p$ | Common shift, default $c=1$ |
| `sparse` | $0$ | $\delta e_1$ | Mean difference in the first coordinate |
| `dense` | $0$ | $\delta\mathbf1_p/\sqrt p$ | Mean difference spread across all coordinates |

Defaults use $\delta\in\{1,2\}$. Both directions have $\|\mu_Y-\mu_X\|_2=\delta$, independent of $p$. Edit `mean_deltas`, `mean_directions`, and `common_shift` in the YAML. Baseline and common-shift controls are always included; do not add 0 to `mean_deltas`. The six default mean settings produce **180 × 6 × 2 = 2160 summary rows**.

Within each base scenario and replicate, mean settings share baseline samples and permutations. Sample covariances use denominator $m-1$. Each permutation selects $m$ pooled observations for one group and assigns the remainder to the other, then recomputes both sample covariances. Raw groups are pooled **without first centering them separately**, preserving the mean difference under study. The test retains the plus-one upper-tail $p$ value and rejection rule $\widehat p\leq\alpha$.

A common shift preserves observed and permutation statistics up to floating-point error. Separate shifts preserve the observed statistic but can change the permutation distribution and rejection rate. **Unequal means are outside the paper's common-mean null model.** These are sensitivity checks under equal covariance, not evidence that the existing theorem covers unequal means. Identical baseline distributions with unequal means are not labeled exchangeable.

## Running and outputs

Knit uses the YAML defaults: $R=500$, $B=500$, and $\alpha=0.05$, with at most 7 workers and single-threaded BLAS per worker. At fixed $R$ and $B$, six mean settings require about six times the baseline test computation. Adjust `R` for rejection-rate precision and `B` for permutation precision.

Rendering requires `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, and Pandoc. Keep this Rmd beside `R/` and `data/`. Shared generation and tests are in `R/simulation_core.R`; paired simulations and summaries are in `R/mean_shift_runner.R`. `R/mean_shift_reference.R` reads `data/manuscript_reference.csv`, also used by report 01. Reference counts and unrounded MCSEs are recovered from the saved rates using $R=1000$.

To match the Tables 1–3 parameters, set $R=B=1000$ and retain `alpha: 0.05` and `seed: 20260925`. Setting `mean_deltas: !r c(0.5, 1, 2)` gives eight mean settings and 2880 summary rows. Knit explicitly passes all YAML parameters; direct R function defaults retain the historical configuration.

Start with this smoke check to verify execution; it cannot assess type I error.

```{r smoke-command, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "03_mean_shift_sensitivity.Rmd",
  params = list(profile = "smoke", R = 3, B = 39, workers = 1),
  output_file = "03_mean_shift_sensitivity_smoke.html"
)
```

Results are saved in a run directory under `../simulation_results/mean_shift/`. With default `resume: true`, checkpoints are saved every `checkpoint_every` replicates (default 10). Matching source files, scientific parameters, and R environment allow resumption. Changing `workers` affects neither seeds nor the run directory.

Run identifiers hash the full Rmd, loaded R modules, and reference CSV. Editing them creates a new directory; each run preserves their directory structure in a source snapshot. Avoid concurrent runs with identical parameters. Use `resume: false` for a fresh output directory.

| Output | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `summary.csv` | Rejection rate, MCSE, 95% Wilson interval, and failure count by base scenario, mean setting, and $k$ |
| `paired_vs_baseline.csv` | Rejection-rate difference from the paired zero-mean baseline and paired MCSE |
| `translation_diagnostics.csv` | Shift effects on observed statistics, permutation statistics, and decisions |
| `baseline_vs_tables123.csv` | New zero-mean baseline versus saved Tables 1–3 reference values |
| `replicates.csv` | Replicate statistics, $p$ values, decisions, status, and seeds |
| `failures.csv` | Replicates with status other than `ok`; header only if none |
| `mean_design.csv`, `mean_vectors.csv` | Mean settings and coordinate means |
| `checkpoints/`, `configuration.*`, source snapshot, `sessionInfo.txt` | Resume files, configuration, source files, and R environment |

The paired MCSE is $\operatorname{sd}(I_{\rm shift}-I_{\rm baseline})/\sqrt R$, where $I$ is the rejection indicator for the same replicate. It differs from an independent-simulation difference standard error. Wilson intervals are per-scenario intervals without multiplicity adjustment. Failed computations are recorded, not counted as nonrejections; scenarios with failures do not report a primary rate for the full experiment. `COMPLETED.txt` marks completion of all requested replicates; also check summary `failed` counts and replicate `status`.

## Results

```{r run-experiment, message=TRUE}
grid <- ms_grid(params$profile)
result <- ms_run(grid, R = params$R, B = params$B, alpha = params$alpha, seed = params$seed,
  workers = params$workers, mean_deltas = unlist(params$mean_deltas), mean_directions = unlist(params$mean_directions),
  common_shift = params$common_shift, output_root = params$output_root, resume = params$resume,
  checkpoint_every = params$checkpoint_every, input_path = .slads_input_path)
```

Output: `r result$directory`. Completed `r nrow(grid)` base scenarios and produced `r nrow(result$summary)` scenario/test results.

```{r rate-preview}
cols <- c("p", "m", "covariance", "pair", "mean_id", "method", "type1_error_rate", "mcse", "ci_low",
  "ci_high", "failed")
stopifnot(all(cols %in% names(result$summary)))
knitr::kable(head(result$summary[cols], 16), digits = 4, caption = "Rejection-rate preview; full results in summary.csv")
```

```{r paired-preview}
paired_cols <- c("p", "m", "covariance", "pair", "mean_id", "delta", "k", "paired_rate_difference",
  "paired_mcse", "matched_valid")
knitr::kable(head(result$paired[result$paired$mean_id != "baseline", paired_cols], 12), digits = 4,
  caption = "Paired comparison with the zero-mean baseline (first 12 rows)")
```

```{r translation-checks}
dc <- result$diagnostics[result$diagnostics$mean_id == "common_shift", ]
diagnostic_preview <- data.frame(check = c("Common shift: valid permutation-sequence comparisons by k",
  "Common shift: p-value mismatches", "Common shift: rejection-decision mismatches", "Common shift: maximum absolute permutation-statistic change",
  "All mean settings: maximum absolute observed-statistic change"), value = c(sum(dc$common_permutation_comparisons),
  sum(dc$common_p_value_mismatches), sum(dc$common_reject_mismatches), ms_max_finite(dc$max_common_permutation_statistic_abs_diff),
  ms_max_finite(result$diagnostics$max_observed_statistic_abs_diff)))
knitr::kable(diagnostic_preview, caption = "Translation checks; differences near machine precision may occur")
```

```{r baseline-reference}
baseline_check <- ms_compare_paper_reference(result)
write.csv(baseline_check, file.path(result$directory, "baseline_vs_tables123.csv"), row.names = FALSE,
  na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
knitr::kable(head(baseline_check[c("p", "m", "covariance", "pair", "method", "new_rate", "paper_rate",
  "rate_difference", "same_simulation_parameters")], 12), digits = 4, caption = "Zero-mean baseline versus Tables 1–3 (first 12 rows)")
```

`paper_rate` contains historical reference CSV values, shown separately from new estimates. Matching simulation parameters means $R=B=1000$, $\alpha=0.05$, and seed `20260925`. Differences after changing parameters do not indicate reproduction failure. The run configuration records the R version, platform, and RNG settings.
